title.narrative: Accelerating city climate action implementation through Innovate4Cities, engagement with the Urban Transitions Mission, and multi-level governance support

description.narrative:
PROJECT DESCRIPTION
The partnership will advance innovation and multi-level governance in urban climate adaptation and mitigation, building on the existing expertise and complementarity of both agencies, as well as past collaboration between GCOM and UN-Habitat. It will support the adaptation and climate-proofing agendas of cities and contribute to resilient zero-carbon urban development. Acknowledging the growing need for climate-related programmes in cities, climate-resilient, sustainable and low-carbon urban transformations are core to UN Habitat’s strategy and priority initiatives – and align with the soon-to-be-released City Research Agenda and updated Global Research and Action Agenda. The role of innovation in urban climate mitigation and adaptation Knowledge transfer and innovation are key to advancing international and local climate agendas, scaling up climate initiatives and spreading best practice progress in social and ecological policy, disaster risk management, green/blue infrastructure and social policy, which are paramount to achieve climate targets. Innovation can help to reinforce the sustainability and resilience of urban systems, while decoupling energy usage from economic growth / decarbonizing the economy, and reducing vulnerabilities. For example, incorporating socioeconomic interventions or nature-based solutions in mitigation or adaptation initiatives can lead to multiple synergies in terms of sustainable development gains and biodiversity targets. Innovation policy packages have furthermore helped to address distributional, environmental and social impacts of the diffusion of low-emission technologies and supported just transitions to low-carbon futures. Furthermore, partnerships, conferences and networks can be essential to facilitate learning, spread best practice approaches and scale successful urban innovations from one to multiple locations. The Innovate4Cities Conference, hosted jointly with the Global Covenant of Mayors, brought together nearly 7,000 participants and 880 speakers in 190 sessions, and resulted in an enhanced Global Research and Action Agenda (GRAA) on local climate action. Finally, innovation is core to UN-Habitat’s 2020-23 strategic plan, aiming to reposition UN-Habitat as a center of excellence and innovation and shaping the global discourse and agenda on sustainable urban development.
Multi-level governance for low-emission and resilient climate action Cities have been recognized for their crucial role in climate action, as they drive implementation on the ground, are at the frontlines of adaptation and mitigation, and foster innovation. However, this requires credible climate commitments that are facilitated by compelling, trusted and inclusive governance systems at all levels, from national to local institutions. The IPCC has identified many core barriers to successful climate action in cities are linked to issues with political systems and governmental capacity, including the lack of understanding social vulnerability and community strengths, the absence of integrated planning and appropriate institutions, as well as insufficient or inappropriate funding schemes. Enabling and accelerating resilience and decarbonization strategies in cities needs a coordinated integration of sectors, strategies and innovation from local to national actors. Multilevel action can be key to enhance social and economic system change and support inclusive and sustainable climate action in the context of interconnected risks and multiple pressures. Launched at COP 26, the GCoM Multilevel Climate Action Playbook highlighted the enabling environment needed to produce robust ‘Regional and Local Contributions’ that can inform, bolster, and raise the profile of Nationally Determined Contributions and national policy processes with a focus on climate. The Playbook is underpinned by the understanding that national commitment and action on climate is made stronger when accounting for the efforts of their cities and local governments. UN Habitat, in partnership with UNDP, and the GCoM alliance of partners has strengthened its capacity for policy advisory services to national governments and implementation support of national programs at the local level.
APPROACH
The project will facilitate urban climate change innovation and provide policy advisory service for multi-level climate action governance. The project will build on UN-Habitat’s existing relationship with GCoM to set the agenda at international research, events and conferences, including the IPCC special report, World Urban Forum 11 and COP27.
